sources.entry: The seven programming ur-languages: ALGOL, Lisp, ML, Self, Forth, APL, Prolog

summary.title: The seven programming ur-languages
summary.one_liner: Learn that most programming languages descend from seven core "ur-languages" (ALGOL, Lisp, ML, Self, Forth, APL, Prolog), and that switching between families, not between similar languages, is the real learning effort.
takeaways: Most mainstream languages (C, Java, Python, JavaScript) share the ALGOL ur-language's patterns of assignments, loops and functions.
Each of the seven ur-languages has distinct fundamental patterns; learning one within the same family is easy, while switching families takes significant effort.
Recommended path: learn one ALGOL-family language well, then SQL (Prolog family), then one new language from an unfamiliar family each year.
summary.summary: The author argues that programming languages should be grouped by their fundamental patterns rather than by syntax, identifying seven ur-languages: ALGOL, Lisp, ML, Self, Forth, APL and Prolog. For each, the essay covers defining characteristics, example languages, and history, with short code samples illustrating looping, recursion, prefix syntax, stack operations, array operators and logic facts. It also traces how ideas migrated between families. It closes with practical advice on which families to learn and in what order, noting that exact language choices matter less than broadening exposure.
